additional_concerns: All 12 required pairs are retained. NOT_APPLICABLE findings concern the exact gift questions; they do not establish overall candidate correctness or authorize pruning these source claims.

Offering and promotion are substantive conditions in some candidates but scope conditions in others. Consequently, an absent offer or promotional link can produce FALSE in one candidate and OUT_OF_SCOPE in another. Unknown scope also blocks results that a result-level conjunction could resolve. These alternatives require an explicit interface decision.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-level promotional connection with an existential non-discount gift predicate. Unless the supplied classifications connect the same gift component to the qualifying promotion, unrelated components could jointly produce an unsupported prohibition.

The circular defines distributors as intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds, while paragraph 10 describes specific investment products and product types. Broader actor definitions and narrower product definitions in individual candidates require reconciliation with that context; their equivalence is not established.

Gift classification remains a supplied judgment. Paragraph 9 says guaranteed returns or incentives may be gifts; neither their existence nor structured-product classification automatically establishes or excludes gift status.

The offer-attribution statements in node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b go beyond the explicit source concerning third-party funding and fulfilment. Offering does not require completed payment, but attribution in every third-party arrangement remains unverified.

Independent gift-standard review requires the absent Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC FAQs issued on 30 September 2010, identified by footnotes 2 and 3. No supplied external dependency IDs identify these authorities.

Independent review of the broader advertising regime requires the absent Code of Conduct paragraph 2.3, Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes, and supplementary FAQs and guidance identified by footnote 4. The narrow advertising claims remain directly supported by the circular.

The advertising duties retain the service context established by paragraphs 3 and 15–16. They do not establish a blanket prohibition on mentioning positive or guaranteed returns. The deposit-parallel claim captures one duty, not every deposit-like implication prohibited by paragraph 17.
The packet does not establish a concrete effective-date interval or the applicable temporal versions of incorporated authorities. The candidates' temporal-basis wording does not supply that evidence.

Passing the selected gift control, or returning FALSE for gift prohibition, establishes no permission under section 103 and no overall advertising or regulatory compliance. Conversely, separate statutory and advertising duties must not silently become additional gift conditions.
